evidence: Receiving DO2 step drop from 11.69 mg/L (46.0 h) to 4.30 mg/L (46.2 h), unlike any source batch
DO2 decline continues to 2.74 mg/L at 52.0 h, approaching the 2.0 mg/L minimum with ~-0.05 mg/L/h slope
P assay at 48 h = 2.45 g/L (up from 0.99 g/L at 36 h): culture actively producing; stop or strong feed cut would sacrifice product mass
Source batches show self-recovering DO2 dips only with aeration step-ups (e.g., 24 h dip recovered after 28 h step-up); receiving 46 h event shows no recovery after 6 h
No evidence from KEEP trend that constraint violation will be avoided without intervention
args.rationale: The receiving vessel suffered an abrupt oxygen-transfer deficit at ~46 h: DO2 fell from ~11.7 to ~4.3 mg/L in a single interval and has since declined monotonically to 2.74 mg/L at the 52 h decision point, on track to breach the 2.0 mg/L minimum within ~10-15 h. Product is still actively being produced (P: 0.99 g/L at 36 h to 2.45 g/L at 48 h), so retaining product mass rules out a stop or a severe feed cut. The combined bounded intervention (feed x0.8, air x1.15) reduces oxygen uptake demand while adding transfer headroom, addressing both sides of the OUR-vs-OTR imbalance and mirroring the aeration step-ups that restored DO2 in the source batches. Waiting for an extra assay is unnecessary: the DO2 sensor trend is unambiguous and time-critical.
args.uncertainty: Hidden transfer and kinetic parameters are unavailable; the +15% air and -20% feed changes may not fully reverse the decline (if the deficit is larger than estimated) or may overshoot, slowing production more than needed. Sensor noise (~±0.2 mg/L) is small relative to the observed 9 mg/L step drop, so the deficit diagnosis is robust, but the post-intervention DO2 trajectory should be monitored and escalated (stronger reduction) if DO2 keeps falling below ~2.5 mg/L.
